summary: Master reproductive justice policy analysis and rights-based advocacy. Learn the SisterSong framework and impact assessment tools. Enroll today.
lede: Reproductive justice policy training helps professionals assess how laws and health programs affect bodily autonomy and equitable care. It is designed for people who develop, implement, or evaluate policies connected to reproductive health and human rights, with practice in intersectional legislative analysis, equity-focused budget reviews, and community-centered program design. The syllabus also covers advocacy planning, impact assessment, and digital health data governance.
audienceIntro: This program is tailored for mid-to-senior level professionals responsible for designing, implementing, or evaluating policies that intersect with reproductive health and human rights.
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 3 years of experience in public health, law, social policy, or advocacy. A basic understanding of human rights principles is expected; no prior legal or coding expertise is required, though familiarity with data spreadsheets is beneficial.
